April 16, 2025 - Testimony in support of LD 1438:
"Resolve, Regarding Deer Hunting on Mount Desert Isiond"
Good afternoon Senator Baidacci, Representative Roberts, and members of the Joint Standing
Committee On Inland Fisheries and Wildlife. Thank you for the opportunity to testify today. My
name is Representative Billy Bob Faulkingham, and I serve as the House Republican Leader. l
represent House District 12, which includes the towns of Franklin, Gouldsboro, Hancock, Sorrento, Sullivan, Winter Harbor, and Steuben. i'm here to speak in support of LD 1438 -- "ResoIve, Regarding
Deer Hunting on Mount Desert Island. "
This bill is a common-sense step toward addressing a longstanding and increasingly serious issue on Mount Desert Island (MDI): the overpopulation of white-tailed deer. By directing the Commissioner of inland Fisheries and Wildlife to adopt rules allowing deer hunting on the island, LD 1438 will help restore ecological balance, improve public safety, and support better public health outcomes.
The white-tailed deer population on MDi has reached unsustainable levels. These elevated numbers
are leading to:
0 Severe forest regeneration issues: Deer are consuming young tree saplings, especially native species like cedar, maple, and ash, preventing natural forest regrowth and altering forest
structure.
0 Negative impacts on native plant communities and biodiversity: Over browsing is threatening rare plant species and displacing understory vegetation that supports birds, insects, and other
wildlife.
Overpopulation of deer also increases the risks of human-deer conflicts. Results can include a significant rise in deer-vehicle collisions, causing vehicle damage, injury, and in some cases, fatalities.
High deer densities are also directly correlated with elevated populations of ticks that transmit Lyme disease and other tick-borne illnesses. Maine is already one of the states with the highest rates of Lyme disease in the country, and residents and visitors on MDI are especially at risk due to the close proximity of deer to homes, trails, and public spaces.
This is not the first time MD] communities have recognized the need for deer population control. Towns such as Bar Harbor and Mount Desert have established deer reduction committees or explored controlled hunts and fertility control programs. However, without broader authority granted
by the state and support from IFW, local efforts have been limited in scope and effectiveness.

Additionally, other coastal communities in Maine have successfully implemented managed hunts to control deer populations, such as on lslesboro and Peaks Island, where special seasons and expanded hunting rules have been used to mitigate the very same problems we're seeing on MDI.
LD 1438 takes a necessary and measured approach to addressing a complex but urgent issue. By empowering the Commissioner of IFW to adopt hunting rules for MDI under existing law, the state can help communities regain control of an environmental and public health challenge that has grown beyond their capacity to manage alone.
This legislation reflects a responsible wildlife management strategy, respects landowner rights, and
supports both ecological health and public safety. I urge you to vote "Ought to Pass" on LD 1438.
Thank you for your time, and I'd be happy to answer any questions.
Respectfully,
mg M
Rep. Billy Bob Faulkingham House Republican Leader

Testimony of Representative Holly Eaton in opposition to LD 1438: Resolve, Regarding Deer Hunting on Mount Desert Island
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlife

Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts, and esteemed members of the Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee, my name is Representative Holly Eaton, and I represent House District 15, which includes part of Mount Desert Island. I am submitting this written testimony in opposition to LD 1438.
This bill seeks to open Mount Desert Island to deer hunting, lifting a ban that has been in place since 1905. While I understand the concerns regarding deer overpopulation, I am deeply concerned about the process through which this legislation was introduced. Neither I, Representative Gary Friedmann (who represents the other part of MDI), nor Senator Nicole Grohoski were consulted prior to the submission of this bill.
Since the bill was introduced, Senator Grohoski, Representative Friedmann, and I have worked together to contact each of the municipalities on Mount Desert Island to ensure they were aware of LD 1438 and had an opportunity to weigh in. We heard unanimously that, while communities are open to engaging in future discussions around deer management, they are not currently comfortable with this legislation moving forward.
Representative Friedmann will be present at today's hearing and is welcome to share that he and I are aligned in our position. We are both open to working collaboratively with municipalities, the department, and other stakeholders to explore solutions if needed--but this bill is not the appropriate vehicle for those changes.
It's also important to note that current law already allows for local governing bodies to initiate changes to hunting regulations under Title 12, Section 11402, Subsection 4. That process respects the authority of local communities and should be upheld.
For these reasons, I respectfully urge the committee to vote "Ought Not to Pass" on LD 1438.

TESTIMONY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
NEITHER FOR NOR AGAINST L.D. 1438
"Resolve, Regarding Deer Hunting on Mount Desert Island"
Presented by Representative FAULKINGHAM of Winter Harbor.
DATE OF HEARING: Wednesday, April 16, 2025
Good morning, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee. I am Nate Webb, Wildlife Division Director at the
Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, speaking on behalf of the Department, neither for nor against L.D. 1438.
This resolve directs the Commissioner of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife to adopt rules
opening Mount Desert Island (MDI) to deer hunting.
Various hunting regulations have existed relating to Mount Desert Island over the years. The present ban on deer hunting was implemented by the 85"` Maine Legislature, and
reference to a closed season on deer on MDI first appeared in the 1931-1932 regulations
book. The precise reason for the ban and all of the conversations that precipitated it are subject to debate at this point, but suffice it to say, some island residents- whether seasonal or year~round, were very displeased with the occurrence of deer hunting on the
island. Objections to deer hunting on MDI in the present day (and presumably at the time
of the ban) included proximity to the National Park, safety concems, and the desire to
maintain the tranquility and natural state of the island. We will note that the ban included
only deer hunting, and the island is currently open to the hunting of other species.
Efforts to open the island to deer hunting have occurred periodically. Proponents of opening the island to deer hunting contend that deer have become too abundant, the island's natural habitat is being damaged by deer, and deer are causing damage to
omamental plants and gardens. Historically, MDIFW has provided information and
technical assistance to towns that wish to investigate the issue of allowing deer htmting, and on some occasions, towns have shown considerable support for allowing hunting or targeted deer reduction efforts. In all cases, however, the support has fallen short of the opposition, and towns have been unable to agree on a functional path forward.

10044630:
TESTIMONY OF SUSANNA RICHER IN OPPOSITION TO
LD 1438 Resolve, Regarding Deer Hunting on Mount Desert Island Committee On Inland Fisheries and Wildlife April 16, 2025
Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts, and distinguished members of the Committee:
I am writing in strong opposition to LD 1438 Resolve, Regarding Deer Hunting on Mount Desert Island. LD 1438 Is unnecessary and undermines the will and control of the citizens who live on this island. Below are the reasons why.
 All of Mount Desert Island has been closed to deer hunting for over a century due to special law passed by the Maine legislature at the request of island residents.
 Existing laws already allow municipalities to initiate changes to hunting regulations. If the residents of Mount Desert Island wish to open up the island to deer hunting, they could decide to do so, or not, at the town level. For instance, in 2014, in response to the deer herd control task force findings, the citizens of Bar Harbor voted down a proposed plan to legalize deer hunting.
 There are many alternatives to hunting to control the deer population, manage "nuisance" deer, and reduce car/ deer collisions. These include:
o Reduce hunting of predators such as coyotes to keep deer populations in check o Install fencing, solar motion detector lights, and/or natural barriers (e.g. blackberry bushes)
to protect gardens o Wrap metal flashing around the base of trees o Invest in wildlife crossings (the state recently received $9.3 million for such projects) or
roadside fencing at problem areas and drive the speed limit to avoid deer/ car collisions.
 Additionally, property owners can apply for special permits from state game wardens to hunt deer on their own land if they meet spatial requirements and can prove a nuisance problem.
As a result of all the above reasons, this bill is unnecessary and circumvents local control of the citizens that live on this island. Please vote ought not to pass on LD 1438.
Thank you,
Susanna Richer Portland ME
